chapter_theme: Reviling Siva (சிவ நிந்தை): those who scorn the Lord as easy fall as a parrot falls to a cat; gods and asuras who opposed him perished, and even Vedic Brahmins who dwell on pleasure forget him. Enmity toward him, even feigned, rebounds many times over.

526.reading: To those in whose minds clear knowledge has come, who melt in longing for the heavenly city, he is easy; if base people scorn the Lord for being easy, they go down like a parrot to a cat.
526.nuance: எளியன் (easy, accessible) is both his gift to the devoted and the excuse of the scornful. கிளியொன்று பூஞையால் may also mean that the scorned Lord is as a parrot to the cat's eyes, but the fall of the scorner fits கீழதுவாகுமே.

527.reading: Gods and asuras who withered have all perished, not knowing the knowledge that stands in truth; the First Lord, from whom ripe nectar wells up, cannot be borne except by those who have become calm.
527.nuance: தளிந்தவர் is uncertain: perhaps 'those cooled and settled' or 'those who have drawn near'. The ripe nectar may recall the churning of the sea.

528.reading: Through that enmity asuras and gods waged their good war and perished midway; whatever enmity they bear, they do not reach the Lord, and even a false enmity against him becomes one tenfold.
528.nuance: நற்பகை (good enmity) is ironic or refers to the war of gods and asuras. The last line may mean the Lord answers even a pretended hostility tenfold, or that one false enmity grows into ten.

529.reading: Because they dwell on pleasure and the sulking of women and have that mingled in their very bodies, even those who are Vedic Brahmins abandon thought of the Lord who abides in the rule that says 'we are Vikirta'.
529.nuance: விகிர்தன் (the one unlike all, a name of Siva) and நாம் என்கின்ற நீதி are hard to fix: the line may refer to the Lord as known in the Veda or to a teaching of identity with him. The verse's target is plain: learning does not save those lost in pleasure.

links.note: 229 says Brahmins who heard Vedanta and kept their craving have not truly heard it; 529 says Vedic Brahmins who dwell on pleasure forget the Lord. In both, Vedic standing is undone by desire.

526 says the Lord is easy (எளியன்) to those of clear knowledge and that the base who scorn him for it fall like a parrot to the cat; 392 calls him the Lord whose kindness is easy (நயன் எளிதாகிய நம்பன்) and the way to the fruit easy. Read together, the easiness 392 praises is the very thing 526 says the base mistake for smallness.

526 warns against scorning the Lord because he is easy (எளியன் என்று ஈசனை நீசர் இகழில்); 1578 shows the same error before the guru, where the utter fools say of Siva come as guru 'he is one of us' (நமர் என்பர) while the meritorious bow. Both locate the offence in despising the divine for having come near.

527 says gods and asuras perished (விளிந்தவர்) not knowing the knowledge that stands in truth; 528 opens with அப்பகையாலே, 'through that enmity', and names their war as the cause: they perished midway and did not reach the Lord. 528 supplies the reason 527 only implies.

529 says even Vedic Brahmins (வேதியராயும்) lost in pleasure and women's sulking abandon thought of the Lord; Kural 134 says a forgotten Veda can be learned again but a Brahmin's birth is ruined when conduct fails (பிறப்பொழுக்கம் குன்றக் கெடும்). Both deny that Vedic standing protects one whose conduct has gone.
